name: Jeffrey Cheah
current_role: Founder and Chairman, Sunway Group; Founder and Chancellor, Sunway University; Founder and Trustee, Jeffrey Cheah Foundation
profile: Malaysian tycoon who in 1974 left a job as an accountant at an auto assembly plant to buy a near-mined-out tin-mining company, then turned the land into Sunway City. Sunway now spans property, healthcare (Sunway Healthcare IPO'd in March 2026), construction, education and more; his children Sarena, Adrian and Evan work in the group.
interesting_fact: His Jeffrey Cheah Foundation, which owns Sunway University, is on track to award more than RM1 billion in scholarships and grants by 2026 - the largest such education foundation in Malaysia.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up in Pusing, a small tin-mining town in Perak about 200 km north of Kuala Lumpur; seeing the scarred mining land there shaped his idea to rehabilitate the ex-mine that became Sunway City. He also co-chairs Mission 4.7, a UN SDSN education-for-sustainability initiative.
notes: Go through Sunway Group Corporate Communications (media form). Sunway warns of impersonation scams - only use official sunway.com.my channels. Sunway hosts annual media nights and is press-friendly; energy/infrastructure angle via Sunway's autonomous transport and electric aviation plans (Oct 2026).

name: Brad Garlinghouse
profile: Kansas-born executive (b. 1971) who held senior roles at @Home, Dialpad, Yahoo (SVP running Homepage, Flickr, Mail, Messenger) and AOL, then ran Hightail (ex-YouSendIt). Joined Ripple as COO in 2015 and became CEO around end-2016; his wealth comes from Ripple equity and XRP. He continues to lead Ripple's global payments, custody and RLUSD stablecoin push.
interesting_fact: As a Yahoo SVP in 2006 he wrote the internal 'Peanut Butter Manifesto' memo, warning Yahoo was spreading itself too thin like peanut butter; it leaked to the Wall Street Journal and became a Silicon Valley strategy classic.
deep_cut_fact: He told Fortune his interest in technology began growing up in Kansas when his dad brought home a Tandy TRS-80 computer.
notes: Very media-accessible, active on X (@bgarlinghouse) and frequent podcast guest. Best route is Ripple's press team form. Avoid the long SEC-litigation saga as a hook.

name: Nadir Godrej
current_role: Chairperson, Godrej Industries Group (Godrej Industries, Godrej Consumer Products, Godrej Properties, Godrej Agrovet)
profile: Mumbai industrialist (b. 1951), younger brother of Adi Godrej, trained as a chemical engineer (MIT, Stanford) with a Harvard MBA, who joined the family business four-plus decades ago. After the 2024 family split he chairs the Godrej Industries Group - four listed companies with ~$6.1bn revenue spanning consumer goods, chemicals, real estate and agri.
interesting_fact: A published poet, he often delivers business speeches entirely in verse; his first collection, 'Life and Other Poems', appeared in 1992 and he has done joint poetry readings with novelist Vikram Seth.
deep_cut_fact: He started at IIT Bombay but transferred after one year to MIT for chemical engineering; he speaks six languages including Russian and French, is known for a love of mathematics, and is a Chevalier of France's Legion of Honour.

public_contacts.value: Guest appearance: 'Business and Poetry with Nadir Godrej' on AND is the Future podcast

notes: Approachable and has done podcasts before (sustainability angle; Godrej is a WBCSD member). A poetic hook in an outreach note would land well. Route via Godrej Industries media desk.

name: Cai Kui
current_role: Founder/owner, Junson Capital (Hong Kong single-family office); major shareholder of Longfor Group (no executive role)
profile: Co-founded Chongqing developer Longfor Group with then-wife Wu Yajun in the 1990s and served as vice chairman until 2009; he left management after their 2012 divorce but retains a large Longfor stake. In 2013 he set up Junson Capital in Hong Kong, a family office investing in real estate, fixed income, PE and venture (e.g. biotech Full-Life's Series C in 2025).
interesting_fact: Before property, he made his first pot of money trading stocks in Shenzhen and in 1993 founded Chongqing Yatai Industry & Trade, which worked on developing fast battery chargers.
deep_cut_fact: He studied communications engineering at Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics, and his Yatai company was one of the original investors (RMB 500k) in the 1993 building-materials firm that became the forerunner of Longfor.
notes: Extremely private; virtually no interviews or public profile. Junson Capital site (junsoncapital.com) was unreachable when checked; no published press contact found. Alive status not independently confirmed (still on 2026 Forbes real-time list). Avoid divorce topic. Low-probability podcast guest.

name: Ramon Ang
current_role: Chairman and CEO, San Miguel Corporation; President and CEO, Top Frontier Investment Holdings
profile: Tondo-raised mechanical engineer (b. 1954) who rose from fixing and dealing used Japanese engines to running San Miguel, the Philippines' oldest conglomerate. He steered it from beer and food into power, fuel (Petron), cement and infrastructure - including the $15bn New Manila International Airport in Bulacan, the NAIA revamp and a $3.3bn LNG hub in Batangas.
interesting_fact: Per a widely told account, he met San Miguel chairman Danding Cojuangco at a car repair shop: when the mechanics couldn't diagnose Cojuangco's sports car, Ang identified the defect and was hired on the spot as his mechanic - the start of a decades-long partnership.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his mechanical engineering degree from Far Eastern University as a working student while helping in his father's auto repair shop on Jose Abad Santos Street in Tondo; FEU gave him an honorary doctorate in business engineering in 2018. He is also a former racing driver and vintage-car restorer.
notes: Highly relevant to energy (SMC Global Power, LNG, Petron) and infrastructure. Gives frequent press conferences in Manila. No dedicated press email published; SMC Corporate Affairs Office (main line +63 2 8632 3000) is the media route; IR email listed as fallback.

name: Jenny Love Meyer
current_role: Executive Vice President and Chief Culture Officer, Love's Travel Stops & Country Stores
profile: Daughter of Tom and Judy Love, who founded Love's in 1964 with a $5,000 family loan; the Oklahoma City chain now has 600+ truck stops in 42 states and ~$22bn in sales, run by her brothers Frank and Greg as co-CEOs. She joined the company in 1991 and in 2019 became its first-ever Chief Culture Officer; her wealth stems from the family's ownership stake.
interesting_fact: She was the first person to hold the title of chief culture officer at Love's, created in November 2019, and has described culture as being like the water in an aquarium: always present, but it needs nourishing.
deep_cut_fact: She studied political science at Colorado College, began at Love's in 1991 in business and operational roles, and for years led the company's public/media relations, internal communications and charitable giving; she sits on the Greater Oklahoma City Chamber executive committee.
notes: Speaks at comms/HR conferences (Ragan, NACS), so open to culture/leadership conversations. Energy angle: Love's has expanded into truck EV charging, CNG/RNG and hydrogen fueling. Route via Love's media relations.

name: Xie Zhikun
profile: Founder of Beijing-based Zhongzhi Enterprise Group (est. 1995), who started in timber and real estate before building a large wealth-management/shadow-banking business. He died of a heart attack in Beijing on 18 December 2021, aged 61.
notes: DECEASED 18 Dec 2021 (heart attack, Beijing) - sources: https://www.scmp.com/news/china/politics/article/3160259/chinese-rags-riches-tycoon-xie-zhikun-dies-aged-61 ; https://yicaiglobal.com/news/20211220-03---shares-of-firms-controlled-by-china-zhongzhi-dive-on-founder-sudden-death . Zhongzhi later collapsed and entered liquidation (2023-24). Not a podcast candidate.

name: Gérard Déprez
profile: French executive who took over equipment-rental firm SAM in Brittany in 1986 and built it into Loxam, Europe's No.1 and the world's 4th-largest equipment rental company (~1,120 branches in 30 countries, ~€2.6bn revenue in 2024) through acquisitions such as Lavendon, Cramo Denmark and Finland's Ramirent (2019). He remains chairman, with Stéphane Hénon as managing director.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Loxam grew from a 1967 regional Breton rental outfit into a supplier of equipment for the Paris 2024 Olympic and Paralympic Games.
deep_cut_fact: Before Loxam he was VP of finance at cement maker Ciments d'Origny (Holderbank group) from 1978-83 and a regional director at building-materials firm SOCIMAT; he is an EM Lyon graduate with law and accounting degrees, and chaired the European Rental Association 2005-2013.
notes: Low-profile; rarely gives interviews beyond trade press (KHL, Rental Management). Loxam press releases also route media via FTI Consulting (loxam@fticonsulting.com per search snippets; not verified on a current release). Possible angle: equipment rental for energy/data-center construction and Loxam's carbon trajectory.

name: Marianna Latsis
current_role: Owner/head of Latsco (Latsco Shipping and Latsco Family Office), Greece
profile: Daughter of late Greek shipping tycoon John S. Latsis (b. 1953). After the siblings split the family fortune in 2019, she took the shipping arm, Latsco, which runs ~33 vessels incl. product tankers, gas and LNG carriers, and in 2025 took control of Nasdaq-listed EuroHoldings. Her family office has stakes in GEK Terna, Attiki Odos (10%), Dimand, Helleniq Energy and venture bets (exited Viva Wallet in 2022).
interesting_fact: Latsco's fleet is heavily energy-focused - product tankers, VLCCs, gas and LNG carriers - with dual-fuel Very Large Gas Carriers on order for 2026 delivery.
deep_cut_fact: She funded the 'Nikos Kourkoulos' oncology day-care units in Athens, Thessaloniki and Patras (named for her late husband, the actor), and in 2023 received the Evangelis Zappas Gold Medal from the Olympion and Bequests Committee for her philanthropy.
notes: Very private; essentially no interviews. Son Paris Kassidokostas-Latsis is the more public face of Latsco/EuroHoldings and may be a better route. Energy angle: LNG/LPG shipping, Helleniq Energy, GEK Terna infrastructure.

name: Zhang Ning
current_role: Executive Director and Chairwoman, Red Avenue New Materials Group (彤程新材, Shanghai-listed)
profile: Shanghai-based, Canadian-citizen entrepreneur (about 51) who founded Shanghai Red Avenue Chemical in August 1999, initially distributing rubber additives for tire makers. Red Avenue became a leading tire-chemicals supplier and has since pivoted into semiconductor and display materials such as photoresists and polishing pads; in 2026 it filed for a Hong Kong listing to become A+H dual-listed.
interesting_fact: Red Avenue is one of China's domestic photoresist makers - a strategic chip material long dominated by Japanese suppliers - after she steered the tire-additive business into electronic chemicals from 2020 onward.
deep_cut_fact: She studied biochemical engineering at Beijing Technology and Business University (enrolled 1993) and started the company at about 25, right after graduating; later she earned a doctorate in global financial business management from Arizona State University. In 2020 Red Avenue partnered with BASF to make compostable PBAT polyester.
notes: Rarely interviewed in English media. IR email published in 2025 earnings-call notices for investor questions; HKEX listing prospectus (2026) may list a PR contact. Semiconductor-materials angle relevant to data centers/chips.

name: Family Yaw Teck-seng
current_role: Tan Sri Datuk Amar Yaw Teck Seng - founder of Samling Group (Sarawak timber, plantations, energy); family business run by son Yaw Chee Ming
profile: Listing appears only on Forbes 1996 with no source of wealth; it most likely refers to Sarawak tycoon Yaw Teck Seng, who founded the Samling timber group in 1963 and built it into one of Malaysia's largest timber companies (logging, plywood, plantations, later renewable energy). The family business is jointly run with his son Yaw Chee Ming.
interesting_fact: Samling, founded in 1963, now describes itself as an integrated upstream/downstream timber company with ~4,000 Malaysian employees and has added a renewable-energy business.
deep_cut_fact: The Yaw Teck Seng Foundation, launched 27 October 2008, funds scholarships for disadvantaged Malaysian students and has backed a Penan community education programme and Go Bald for the Sarawak Children's Cancer Society.
notes: Identity inferred (Forbes 1996 'Yaw Teck-seng family', Malaysia); not confirmed by the input. No confirmation found on whether Yaw Teck Seng is alive; he would be very elderly. Samling is the subject of NGO criticism over logging practices - a sensitive topic. Very private family; low podcast fit.

name: Nilima Divi
current_role: Whole-Time Director (Commercial), Divi's Laboratories Ltd, Hyderabad
profile: Daughter of billionaire Murali Divi, founder of Divi's Laboratories, one of the world's largest makers of active pharmaceutical ingredients and a custom-synthesis partner to big pharma; she holds a minority stake. On the board as Director - Commercial, she oversees sourcing and procurement, capital projects, corporate finance and investor relations.
interesting_fact: Divi's Laboratories is among the world's top suppliers of active pharmaceutical ingredients and also does custom manufacturing for global pharma companies.
deep_cut_fact: She joined Divi's in July 2012 after building experience in material-requirement planning and procurement, and holds two master's degrees: international business from the Gitam Institute of Foreign Trade and international finance from the University of Glasgow.
notes: Low public profile; she heads investor relations herself, so IR channel reaches her function. Web search budget ran out mid-lane - role verified only via company site, no press interviews checked.

name: Dennis Gillings
current_role: Founder and former chairman of Quintiles (now IQVIA); philanthropist and life-sciences investor (retired from IQVIA board 2018)
profile: London-born statistician (b. 1944) who moved to UNC Chapel Hill in 1971 to teach biostatistics and in 1982 founded Quintiles to make drug trials faster and more efficient. He took it public in 1994 and built it into the largest clinical-research organization; it merged with IMS Health in 2016 to form IQVIA. Knighted in 2020 for services to dementia and life-sciences research.
interesting_fact: UNC's school of public health - the UNC Gillings School of Global Public Health - is named after him and his first wife Joan, reflecting his roots as a former UNC biostatistics instructor.
deep_cut_fact: He is the son of a London fishmonger; he earned a BSc and PhD in mathematics at the University of Exeter (teaching there while doing his doctorate), and in 1998 endowed the Dennis Gillings Professorship of Health Management at Cambridge.
notes: No personal/family-office contact published that could be verified (web search budget exhausted mid-lane). Spouse Mireille Gillings runs HUYA Bioscience (San Diego) - possible indirect route via the Dennis and Mireille Gillings Foundation, but no official contact page verified. Data-angle: Quintiles/IQVIA is a pioneer of healthcare data.

name: Thomas Dundon
current_role: Chairman & managing partner, Dundon Capital Partners (Dallas); owner/CEO, Carolina Hurricanes (NHL) and Portland Trail Blazers (NBA); chairman, pickleball.com
profile: Dallas financier (b. 1971) who co-founded subprime auto lender Drive Financial, which became Santander Consumer USA; he exited in 2015 with about $700m. Through Dundon Capital Partners he invests in finance, healthcare and real estate, owns the NHL's Carolina Hurricanes, led the $4.2bn Trail Blazers purchase in 2025, and controls pickleball's PPA Tour/UPA.
interesting_fact: His Carolina Hurricanes won the 2026 Stanley Cup - the franchise's first Final appearance since 2006 - eight years after he bought control of the team.
deep_cut_fact: Raised partly in Atco, New Jersey, and Plano, Texas (his father managed pizzerias), his first venture after SMU was a Fort Worth burger restaurant, Izzy's, which closed within a year; he then learned auto lending working in financing at a Chevrolet used-car dealership. He also co-founded Dallas's Trinity Forest Golf Club.
notes: Outspoken and media-accessible (sports/pickleball press). Best routes: Carolina Hurricanes or Trail Blazers communications departments, or PPA Tour/pickleball.com media. Avoid AAF collapse and subprime-lending lawsuits as hooks. No published email verified (search budget exhausted mid-lane).

name: Bill Malhotra
profile: India-born civil engineer who moved to Canada in 1971 at 22, worked at an engineering firm and was chief structural engineer for the City of Ottawa (1977-86) before founding Claridge Homes in 1986. Claridge has built 14,000+ homes, condos and rentals, including the Claridge Icon, Ottawa's tallest building, and is developing projects in the Fort Lauderdale/Pompano Beach area of Florida.
interesting_fact: Claridge's 469-foot Claridge Icon tower is the tallest building in Ottawa.
deep_cut_fact: He named his company after The Claridges, a luxury hotel in New Delhi he used to visit as a child with his father; before going into development he spent nine years as the City of Ottawa's chief structural engineer.
notes: Private, family-run company (sons Neil and Shawn are minority owners); rarely gives national interviews. Route via Claridge Homes head office (505 Preston St, Ottawa; main line published on site). Engineer-turned-developer story fits an entrepreneurship podcast.

name: Bennett Rosenthal
current_role: Co-Founder, Director and Partner, Ares Management; Chairman of the Ares Private Equity Group; Lead Managing Owner, Los Angeles FC (MLS)
profile: Co-founded alternative-investment giant Ares Management (~$596bn AUM) after joining in 1998 from Merrill Lynch, where he was an MD in global leveraged finance. He chairs Ares' private equity business, sits on the Ares executive management committee and on portfolio boards such as CHG Healthcare and TricorBraun, and since January 2023 has been lead managing owner of MLS club LAFC.
interesting_fact: He sits on Ares' Energy Opportunities investment committee as well as its Sports, Media and Entertainment committee, and is lead managing owner of LAFC, whose ownership rotates the lead role every four years.
deep_cut_fact: A double Wharton graduate (BS economics summa cum laude, MBA with distinction), he chairs Wharton's Graduate Executive Board; he chaired Ares Capital's board from its 2004 IPO until 2024, when he became Chairman Emeritus.
notes: Low personal media profile; public appearances mostly via LAFC. Route via Ares media relations (media@aresmgmt.com) or LAFC communications. Ares has a large infrastructure/energy-transition and data-center investing business - relevant angle.

name: Wenxue Wang
current_role: Founder and chairman (as last reported), China Fortune Land Development (CFLD, 华夏幸福), Shanghai-listed
profile: Hebei-born developer (b. 1967) who founded China Fortune Land Development in 1998 and built it into China's largest developer of industrial parks/'new industry cities', notably Gu'an High Tech Park near Beijing; Ping An bought a ~20% stake in 2018. CFLD defaulted on debt in 2021 and has been in a lengthy restructuring; he has dropped off Forbes' list.
interesting_fact: CFLD's Gu'an High Tech Park in Hebei was designated by China's central government as a national demonstration industrial park, a model of its PPP-style 'industrial new town' approach.
deep_cut_fact: After working at the local transport bureau in Langfang, he opened a hotpot restaurant in 1992; it became a popular meeting spot that led him into property refurbishment and then development. He was a member of the 12th CPPCC National Committee.

public_contacts.value: http://www.cfldcn.com (investor relations / 投资者互动 section)

notes: Very low profile and company in debt restructuring since 2021 - sensitive; avoid. Alive status not confirmed (no evidence otherwise found; search budget exhausted). Poor podcast fit.

name: Bill Gross
current_role: Co-founder of PIMCO; private investor managing his own portfolio and family foundation; publishes Investment Outlooks
profile: Co-founded PIMCO in 1971 and became the 'Bond King', running the world's largest bond fund. He left in 2014 for Janus Henderson, retired in 2019, and now manages his personal wealth, writes periodic Investment Outlooks on his website and gives through the William, Jeff and Jennifer Gross Family Foundation.
interesting_fact: The William H. Gross Stamp Gallery at the Smithsonian's National Postal Museum, named for him, is the world's largest gallery dedicated to philately; his collection includes a block of four 1869 24c inverted-center US stamps.
deep_cut_fact: After Duke he served in the Navy (1966-69) as assistant chief engineer aboard the USS Diachenko off Vietnam, and before that briefly played blackjack professionally in Las Vegas - he says he still applies its odds and risk-spreading methods to investing.
notes: Do not confuse with Idealab's Bill Gross (billgross.com). Still comments publicly via outlooks and financial TV. No published contact email or form found on his site; financial-media interviews are the usual route. Avoid PIMCO lawsuit/divorce/neighbor-dispute topics.

name: Albert von Thurn und Taxis
current_role: 12th Prince (Fürst) of Thurn und Taxis; head of the Thurn und Taxis family holdings (Fürst Thurn und Taxis Gesamtverwaltung, Regensburg); racing/rally driver
profile: German aristocrat (b. 1983) who inherited the Thurn und Taxis fortune - built on Europe's historic postal monopoly - at age seven on his father's death in 1990, making him for years the world's youngest billionaire. He took over management of the family business, whose assets include forestry, real estate and Schloss St. Emmeram in Regensburg, and is also a competitive racing and rally driver.
interesting_fact: He won the German ADAC GT Masters sports-car championship in 2010 (after finishing runner-up in 2007/2008) with Reiter Engineering, and has competed in the European Rally Championship since 2016.
deep_cut_fact: After studying economics and theology at the University of Edinburgh, he earned a doctorate in philosophy in 2022 from Rome's Pontifical University of St Thomas Aquinas (Angelicum) with a dissertation titled 'Rational Nature Or Wishful Thinking? Freedom & Rationality in Aquinas And Their Medieval Critique'.
notes: Wealth source listed as '-'; family assets are largely forestry (Thurn und Taxis Forst) and real estate. Press inquiries go through the family's central administration in Regensburg. Motorsport and philosophy are strong hooks; his mother Gloria is the more media-visible family member.
